10901.headingPath: Chapter 24: Information and data management > 24.5 Who is responsible for information and data management?

10902.sentence: The repository and the material it contains should be established, maintained and managed in line with government data standards (see 24.6.1.4 on meeting data management standards) and cyber security requirements (see 24.6.1.5 on protecting information and data security).
10902.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10902.headingPath: Chapter 24: Information and data management > 24.6 How to manage information and data > 24.6.1 What to consider when managing information and data > 24.6.1.1 Organising information and data

10902.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10902.headingPath: Chapter 24: Information and data management > 24.6 How to manage information and data > 24.6.1 What to consider when managing information and data > 24.6.1.1 Organising information and data

10902.sentence: Where the work forms part of a wider portfolio or programme, a consistent approach should be used and, where appropriate, a common repository.
10902.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10902.headingPath: Chapter 24: Information and data management > 24.6 How to manage information and data > 24.6.1 What to consider when managing information and data > 24.6.1.1 Organising information and data

10902.sentence: A clear and simple procedure should be established covering both, to ensure correct storage and handling.
10902.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10902.headingPath: Chapter 24: Information and data management > 24.6 How to manage information and data > 24.6.1 What to consider when managing information and data > 24.6.1.1 Organising information and data

10903.sentence: Minutes should be recorded for all formal meetings relating to the governance and management of the work and held alongside the documents and data submitted to and considered at the meeting.

10903.headingPath: Chapter 24: Information and data management > 24.6 How to manage information and data > 24.6.1 What to consider when managing information and data > 24.6.1.2 Keeping management records

10903.sentence: The minutes should not repeat information in the supporting papers but should include:
10903.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10903.headingPath: Chapter 24: Information and data management > 24.6 How to manage information and data > 24.6.1 What to consider when managing information and data > 24.6.1.2 Keeping management records

10903.sentence: the actions to be taken, by when, by whom and who needs to be informed when the action is complete Minutes should be written up promptly by the meeting secretary and circulated to those present for comment before approval by the chair and then retained as the approved record of the meeting.

10993.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.2 Develop and maintain the communications framework

10993.sentence: The framework should be maintained to address relevant feedback from its use.
10993.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10993.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.2 Develop and maintain the communications framework

10994.sentence: When overseeing communications, the communications manager should consider whether there are any common themes emerging in messaging, audiences or effectiveness of communication and whether further activity is needed in consequence.
10994.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10994.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.3 Oversee communications

10994.sentence: The plan should outline how all audiences are to be communicated with in a coordinated way, with priorities set on those activities which are likely to have the most impact.
10994.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10994.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.3 Oversee communications

10994.sentence: Activities, where significant, should be included in the overall schedule, resource and cost plans for the work (see Chapter 16: Planning).
10994.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10994.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.3 Oversee communications

10994.sentence: Once approved, the communication plan should be managed under change control, as for other parts of the plan (see Chapter 22: Change control).
10994.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10994.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.3 Oversee communications

10994.sentence: The communications framework and plan should be monitored to make sure they remain effective and appropriate as the work proceeds, particularly if things change significantly.
10994.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10994.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.3 Oversee communications

10995.sentence: When planning a campaign, event or activity, objectives should be defined to ensure that those managing and delivering the communications are clear on what is required and so that different elements can be aligned.
10995.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10995.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.4 Plan a campaign, event or activity

10995.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10995.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.4 Plan a campaign, event or activity

10995.sentence: Any analysis should be done in accordance with the Government Functional Standard for Analysis.
10995.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10995.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.4 Plan a campaign, event or activity

10995.sentence: The objectives and audience insights should be used to define the target audience, proposition, messages and channels and techniques to be used.
10995.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10995.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.4 Plan a campaign, event or activity

10995.sentence: To ensure that the campaign or event is realistic, a plan should be developed that includes:
10995.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10995.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.4 Plan a campaign, event or activity

10996.sentence: Once planned, the campaign, event or activity should be delivered with each communication package initiated in accordance with the plan.
10996.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10996.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.5 Deliver campaign, event or activity

10996.sentence: Progress should be monitored in terms of outputs, outtakes and outcomes.
10996.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10996.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.5 Deliver campaign, event or activity

10997.sentence: Evaluation should be conducted to assess the performance and success of the campaign, event or activity.
10997.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10997.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.6 Evaluate campaign, event or activity

10997.sentence: Lessons should be captured, shared and used to improve current and future communication activities (see Chapter 38: Learning from experience ).
10997.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10997.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.6 Evaluate campaign, event or activity

10997.sentence: Communications information and data should be stored for future reference, ensuring that any sensitive data Is handled appropriately (see Chapter 24: Information and data management).
10997.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10997.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.6 Evaluate campaign, event or activity

10998.sentence: The communications manager should agree that the campaign, event or activity has closed and update the communications plan.
10998.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10998.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.7 Close campaign, event or activity

10999.sentence: When no longer needed, the communications framework should be closed down.
10999.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10999.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.8 Close the communications framework

10999.sentence: As part of this, any ongoing need for communication activity following the closure of a programme or project should be identified and transitioned to managers in operations to take on, or alternatively moved to the portfolio level.
10999.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10999.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.8 Close the communications framework

10999.sentence: The effectiveness of communications overall should be evaluated as part of closing the work.
10999.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10999.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.8 Close the communications framework

10999.sentence: Communications information and data should be archived in accordance with the sponsoring organisation’s information and data retention policies (see Chapter 24: Information and data management).
10999.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10999.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.8 Close the communications framework

10999.sentence: Lessons should be captured, shared and used to improve future communication activities (see Chapter 38: Learning from experience ).
10999.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
10999.headingPath: Chapter 27: Communications > 27.6 How to manage communications > 27.6.3 Key activities in managing communications > 27.6.3.8 Close the communications framework

11002.sentence: The strategic workforce planning function in the sponsoring organisation should be engaged as early as possible.
11002.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government

11004.sentence: Resource management should be undertaken in accordance with the Government Functional Standard for People and the Government Functional Standard for Commercial, and advice should be sought from the government human resources and commercial functions as necessary.
11004.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11004.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.4 What is resource management?

11005.sentence: Accountability and responsibility for resource management should be clearly defined within the governance and management framework for the work and reviewed on a regular basis, to avoid duplication or gaps.
11005.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11005.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.5 Who manages resources?

11005.sentence: Roles involving decisions on recruitment or procurement and deployment of resources should therefore be undertaken by substantive employees, other than where this is a defined element of the contract, for example for an interim managerial role, or outsourced to a delivery partner.
11005.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11005.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.5 Who manages resources?

11006.sentence: Human resources requirements should be identified by skill, role type and level, using the relevant professional capability framework where appropriate.
11006.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11006.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.1 Exploring resourcing options

11006.sentence: As resourcing needs are identified, the resource manager should consult the organisation’s strategic workforce planning and facilities teams to explore whether the resources can be met from the existing workforce, as this can offer the quickest and most cost-effective route to meeting them, particularly for small-scale work.
11006.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11006.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.1 Exploring resourcing options

11006.sentence: Where procurement is likely to be required, commercial advice should be sought, and a delivery model assessment should be completed in line with the Government Functional Standard for Commercial and the The sourcing playbook (requires sign in) and The consultancy playbook.
11006.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11006.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.1 Exploring resourcing options

11006.sentence: The decision on how to source resource should be based on:
11006.actor: decision on how to source resource
11006.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11006.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.1 Exploring resourcing options

11006.sentence: The accountabilities and responsibilities of a senior responsible owner mean that this role should be held by a substantive civil servant or public servant.
11006.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11006.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.1 Exploring resourcing options

11007.sentence: The plan should take into account the availability of resources and set the timescales for activities accordingly.
11007.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11007.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.2 Scheduling resources within the plan

11007.sentence: The plan should show when activities are completed and resources are no longer needed, so that they can be reallocated or moved on in an appropriate and considerate way.
11007.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11007.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.2 Scheduling resources within the plan

11008.sentence: A rolling approach to resource forecasting should be taken, which aligns to the wider phased approach to planning.
11008.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11008.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.3 Taking a rolling approach to resource planning

11008.sentence: The resource manager should work with the resource owners to identify any resourcing issues, for example where people are overstretched or under-occupied, and action agreed to address them.
11008.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11008.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.3 Taking a rolling approach to resource planning

11009.sentence: These platforms should be used to monitor resourcing for the work.
11009.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11009.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.4 Ensuring accurate resource monitoring

11009.sentence: Where necessary, advice should be sought from human resources and commercial functions.
11009.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11009.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.4 Ensuring accurate resource monitoring

11009.sentence: Where work is allocated to professional services or consultancy, they should be accountable for planning the resources needed for their work, with the sharing of information and reporting defined in their contract.
11009.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11009.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.1 What to consider when managing resources > 28.6.1.4 Ensuring accurate resource monitoring

11011.sentence: It is also important to understand the wider governance and management framework for the portfolio, programme or project, as this should shape the development of the resource management framework and plan.
11011.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11011.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.2 Preparing to manage resources > 28.6.2.2 Understand the wider governance and management framework

11014.sentence: The approach to resource management should be defined including any processes, methods, tools and techniques to be used.
11014.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11014.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.2 Develop and maintain the resource management framework

11014.sentence: The framework should be maintained to address relevant feedback from its use.
11014.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11014.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.2 Develop and maintain the resource management framework

11014.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11014.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.2 Develop and maintain the resource management framework

11016.sentence: Resource requirements should be identified as part of overall planning (see Chapter 16: Planning) and captured within a resource forecast or workforce plan.
11016.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11016.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.4 Identify resource requirements

11016.sentence: Employee or contingent labour requirements should be estimated for each work activity, both in terms of competency (professional skills, both type and level) and capacity (how many people are needed).
11016.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11016.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.4 Identify resource requirements

11016.sentence: They should be expressed as work days on a full time equivalent (FTE) basis, with estimated costs per FTE, so that resources can be costed.
11016.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11016.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.4 Identify resource requirements

11016.sentence: Requirements for professional services, consultancy and other contracts should be identified separately and included as part of the procurement plan, specified in terms of outputs or outcomes and estimated costs and timescales.
11016.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11016.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.4 Identify resource requirements

11016.sentence: By the time it is approved, the integrated plan (see Chapter 16: Planning) should include a robust, evidence-based resource plan, fully aligned to the schedule, and making provision for risk and contingency.
11016.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11016.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.4 Identify resource requirements

11017.sentence: When deciding on how to source resources, the resource owner should consider whether resources are available in-house, for example from an existing organisational pool, internal recruitment or other resource, or if they need to be sourced externally through recruitment or procurement (see 28.6.1.1 on exploring resourcing options).
11017.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11017.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.5 Source resources

11017.sentence: Plans for sourcing should be agreed as part of portfolio plan and business case approvals, with sourcing activities scheduled to meet resourcing requirements through the life cycle.
11017.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11017.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.5 Source resources

11017.sentence: Recruitment, both internal and external, can be resource intensive, and advice on how best to manage this should be sought from the organisation’s human resources function.
11017.actor: advice on how best to manage this
11017.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11017.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.5 Source resources

11017.sentence: Procuring resources from the external market or through the supply chain requires commercial sourcing expertise, and advice should be sought from the organisation’s commercial function (see Chapter 25: Procurement and contract management).
11017.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11017.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.5 Source resources

11018.sentence: Onboarding should be tailored based on whether the person is new to the delivery or sponsoring organisation.
11018.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11018.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.6 Mobilise resources

11018.sentence: If the person is new to the organisation, the onboarding arrangements should include the organisation’s onboarding process.
11018.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11018.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.6 Mobilise resources

11018.sentence: If the person is not new to the organisation, they should receive a work-specific onboarding experience.
11018.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11018.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.6 Mobilise resources

11018.sentence: The onboarding arrangements for people brought in under contract should cover the requirements of the role as set out in the contract management plan.
11018.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11018.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.6 Mobilise resources

11019.sentence: All employees engaged in the work should have an agreed job description and line manager (and/or an identified task manager), regular performance meetings and annual performance reporting, and a learning and development plan to support their development.
11019.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11019.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.7 Manage resources

11019.sentence: For project delivery professionals, development should be based on the Project delivery capability framework and draw on the learning opportunities within the Government Projects Academy; for other professions, the relevant professional capability framework should be followed.
11019.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11019.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.7 Manage resources

11019.sentence: People employed under contingent labour contracts should have an identified contract manager, are deployed in line with their contract and provided with appropriate induction and support to carry out their role.
11019.actor: People employed under contingent labour contracts
11019.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11019.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.7 Manage resources

11019.sentence: All line managers and contract managers should be aware of their responsibilities and follow the requirements of the Government Functional Standard for People and Government Functional Standard for Commercial at all times.
11019.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11019.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.7 Manage resources

candidateConflicts.sourceTitle: The Digital, Data and Technology Playbook
candidateConflicts.sentence: Additionally, Contract Managers should be aware of their responsibilities to other parties in respect of their own IP.

candidateConflicts.sourceTitle: The Digital, Data and Technology Playbook
candidateConflicts.sentence: Delivery teams, designers and contract managers should be involved early in the process to support commercial and contract design and the transition from procurement to delivery, ensuring adequate time is allocated for each stage.

11020.sentence: If the reusable materials, equipment, and technology are owned by the organisation, they should either be returned, transferred to another user by agreement, or disposed of appropriately, bearing in mind environmental and sustainability considerations (see Chapter 6: Environment and sustainability, and Chapter 37: Use and disposal).
11020.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11020.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.8 Demobilise resources

11020.sentence: When an employee’s role is approaching its end, the individual should be supported in seeking another role.
11020.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11020.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.8 Demobilise resources

11020.sentence: Depending on the nature of the role and assignment, the end of an employee’s role can trigger formal redeployment or redundancy arrangements, and advice should always be sought from the organisation’s human resources function on how to handle this.
11020.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11020.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.8 Demobilise resources

11020.sentence: When demobilising employees, exit interviews should be conducted to understand how the individual has performed in the role and any learning for future assignments.
11020.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11020.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.8 Demobilise resources

11020.sentence: If the resources were procured under contract, the contract manager should ensure that the notice required is provided under the contract and that other contractual arrangements, for example the transition and/or exit plan, are completed before contract end and the release of resources.
11020.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11020.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.8 Demobilise resources

11020.sentence: Where other resources are used, utilisation should be reviewed and documented as part of closing the contract.
11020.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11020.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.8 Demobilise resources

11021.sentence: Once the work has been completed and resource management is no longer needed, the management framework should be either closed or merged into the management framework for the organisation or solution as appropriate.
11021.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11021.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.9 Close the resource management framework

11021.sentence: Information and data should be retained in accordance with the delivery and sponsoring body’s information retention policy (see Chapter 24: Information and data management).
11021.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11021.headingPath: Chapter 28: Resource management > 28.6 How to manage resources > 28.6.3 Key activities in managing resource > 28.6.3.9 Close the resource management framework

11026.sentence: All financial management in government, including for project delivery, should follow HM Treasury’s Managing public money (requires sign in) and its supplementary guidance for accounting officers.
11026.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11026.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.4 What is financial management?

11026.sentence: It should also follow the standards in the Government Functional Standard for Finance, Government Functional Standard for Internal Audit , Government Functional Standard for Counter Fraud , Government Functional Standard for Debt and Government Functional Standard for Grants.
11026.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11026.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.4 What is financial management?

11027.sentence: Accountability and responsibility for financial management should be clearly defined within the governance and management framework and reviewed regularly.
11027.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11027.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.5 Who manages finance? > 29.5.1 Overview

11029.sentence: For programmes and projects in the Government Major Projects Portfolio, an accounting officer assessment must be produced at decision points.
11029.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11029.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.5 Who manages finance? > 29.5.3 Financial roles in project delivery

11029.sentence: A summary of the assessment should be published.
11029.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11029.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.5 Who manages finance? > 29.5.3 Financial roles in project delivery

11030.sentence: Financial management arrangements should be consistent with the sponsoring organisation’s processes and use their financial management and accounting systems wherever possible.
11030.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11030.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.1 Consistency with organisational systems and processes

11030.sentence: Accounting data should be captured consistently across portfolios, programmes and projects so that costs, income, savings and forecasts can be compared and reported at each level.
11030.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11030.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.1 Consistency with organisational systems and processes

11031.sentence: Where this is being considered, advice should be sought from the National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority.
11031.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11031.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.2 Funding sources and availability

11032.sentence: Senior responsible owners should have delegated spending authority within agreed limits and are encouraged to delegate day-to-day spending authority to programme or project managers, who can delegate further if appropriate.
11032.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11032.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.3 Business case approval and spending authorisation

11032.sentence: Spending authority and other delegated authorities, for example on procurement, should be set out in a delegation letter to the senior responsible owner and in individual letters to anyone that authority is further delegated to.
11032.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11032.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.3 Business case approval and spending authorisation

11033.sentence: Financial analysis and modelling should be robust and evidence-based, but where uncertainty exists, it should be stated clearly, with a range of plausible outcomes presented.
11033.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11033.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.4 Managing financial uncertainty

11033.sentence: Specialist advice should be sought on methodology where needed.
11033.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11033.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.4 Managing financial uncertainty

11033.sentence: The financial case should include contingency to cover financial risks and liabilities.
11033.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11033.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.4 Managing financial uncertainty

11033.sentence: The economic case should account for uncertainty and risk in its modelling.
11033.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11033.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.4 Managing financial uncertainty

11033.sentence: As the work progresses and projections become more certain, assumptions should be adjusted and contingency updated.
11033.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11033.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.4 Managing financial uncertainty

11033.sentence: Contingency should be held within the sponsoring organisation, not allocated as part of the budget for the work.
11033.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11033.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.4 Managing financial uncertainty

11033.sentence: Arrangements for managing contingency, drawing it down and accounting for its use should be included in the governance and management framework.
11033.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11033.headingPath: Chapter 29: Finance > 29.6 How to manage finance > 29.6.1 What to consider > 29.6.1.4 Managing financial uncertainty

11201.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.3 Knowing how the solution is to be accepted

11202.sentence: Before transition, everything needed to operate, maintain and use the solution should be ready.

11202.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.4 Checking the completeness of the solution

11202.sentence: Asset data should be verified and prepared for transfer, taking account of security and other statutory requirements.
11202.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11202.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.4 Checking the completeness of the solution

11203.sentence: Transition into use should be planned and managed together with the management of the organisational and societal changes (see Figure 36.1 and Chapter 35: Management of organisational and societal change).

11203.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.5 Working transition and change management together

11203.sentence: An appropriate multi-disciplinary team should be mobilised to plan and carry out the work, with each member providing their expertise.
11203.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11203.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.5 Working transition and change management together

11204.sentence: This should be understood from the start of the programme or project, and defined as a user need, as significant work is often required to achieve continuity.

11204.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.6 Maintaining operations and services during transition

11204.sentence: When the solution replaces an existing or legacy solution, the migration should be planned and managed so that users do not experience any unplanned interruption in services.
11204.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11204.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.6 Maintaining operations and services during transition

11204.sentence: These wider impacts should be considered and planned for as far as possible.
11204.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11204.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.6 Maintaining operations and services during transition

11205.sentence: Where a solution or part of a solution is supplied or operated by a supplier, there are often warranty, guarantee or maintenance clauses in the contract defining how these should be dealt with.

11205.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.7 Knowing how to handle issues after acceptance

11206.sentence: The programme or project manager should be aware of these dynamics and support team members through the transition, for example by helping them prepare for or find new roles.

11206.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.1 What to consider when transitioning the solution > 36.6.1.8 Motivating the team as their work starts to finish

11207.sentence: Planning for transition into use should start, in outline, as soon as the relevant user needs have been identified.
11207.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11207.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.2 Preparing to transition > 36.6.2.1 Overview

11207.sentence: By the time the high-level design is completed, an outline strategy should also be in place and the need for facilities, tools and resources known.
11207.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11207.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.2 Preparing to transition > 36.6.2.1 Overview

11208.sentence: The transition strategy should reflect the user needs, especially the need for operational continuity.
11208.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11208.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.2 Preparing to transition > 36.6.2.2 Agree the transition strategy

11208.sentence: It should be compatible with the change management, verification, validation and integration strategies.
11208.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11208.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.2 Preparing to transition > 36.6.2.2 Agree the transition strategy

11208.sentence: Where possible, most verification and validation should happen before transition into use to reduce the likelihood of faults being discovered during this period.
11208.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11208.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.2 Preparing to transition > 36.6.2.2 Agree the transition strategy

11208.sentence: The expected time and cost constraints associated with the transition strategy should be planned for and requirements factored into procurement and contract documentation.

11208.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.2 Preparing to transition > 36.6.2.2 Agree the transition strategy

11212.sentence: The approach to transition should consider any processes, methods, tools and techniques to be used.

11212.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.2 Develop and maintain the transition management framework

11214.sentence: Detailed planning for transition should follow the approach in the transition strategy and reflect what is needed to handover, operate, maintain and use the solution.
11214.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11214.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.4 Plan for transition into use

11214.sentence: The time units and detail for the plan should reflect the types of work, their criticality and the planning horizon (see Chapter 16: Planning).
11214.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11214.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.4 Plan for transition into use

11214.sentence: The plan should take account of risks associated with transition activities that can be problematic, such as data migration, with schedule buffers placed to avoid overruns.
11214.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11214.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.4 Plan for transition into use

candidateConflicts.sentence: The plan should set out responsibilities for remedying any foreseeable significant risks associated with IP, such as theft or infringements.

11214.sentence: Backout and contingency plans should be developed where needed, with timings and decision points factored into the transition schedule.
11214.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11214.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.4 Plan for transition into use

11214.sentence: If old solutions are to be decommissioned (see Chapter 37: Use and disposal), the plans for that should be integrated with the transition plan and dependencies managed.
11214.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11214.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.4 Plan for transition into use

11215.sentence: Each activity in the transition plan should be tracked, assessed and analysed, if appropriate, collated into reports and take action to address any variances or problems which have been identified (see Chapter 17: Controlling).
11215.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11215.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.5 Transition the solution into use

11215.sentence: Depending on the acceptance criteria, verification and validation of the whole solution, or of an operational part of it if transition is phased, should be carried out in a controlled environment.
11215.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11215.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.5 Transition the solution into use

11215.sentence: This should be followed by a readiness review before a decision is made on whether to hand over the solution formally and release, activate or commission it (see 14.7.2 on gates and decision points).
11215.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11215.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.5 Transition the solution into use

11215.sentence: Full asset management and other data should also be made available, represented as the ‘as built’ reference point (see Chapter 23: Traceability management).
11215.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11215.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.5 Transition the solution into use

11215.sentence: The transition team should normally be kept on during the initial operation of the solution to deal with defects which were not resolved before releasing the solution and to support the new owners, sometimes known as hypercare.
11215.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11215.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.5 Transition the solution into use

11216.sentence: Introduction of the solution and activation of interfaces should be completed and demonstrated in accordance with the acceptance criteria and, where relevant, contracts.

11216.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.6 Manage the results of transition activities

11217.sentence: Once the programme or project has been completed, the management framework should be closed and information archived in accordance with the sponsoring organisation’s information retention policy (see Chapter 24: Information and data management).
11217.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11217.headingPath: Chapter 36: Transition into use > 36.6 How to manage transition > 36.6.3 Key activities in managing transition into use > 36.6.3.7 Close the management framework

11219.sentence: The work should result in a solution which is usable and benefits relevant stakeholders
11219.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11219.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.2 Key points

11219.sentence: How a solution is used and disposed of should be defined in the design.
11219.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11219.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.2 Key points

11222.sentence: Before this, however, they should ensure that accountability for the ongoing use and eventual disposal of the solution has been agreed and is in place.
11222.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11222.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.5 Who manages use and disposal of the solution?

11223.sentence: A full design should include the requirement for partial or full disposal of the solution.
11223.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11223.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.1 What to consider when using and disposing of the solution > 37.6.1.1 The high-level design determines how a solution is used and disposed of

11223.sentence: For partial disposal, the design should accommodate the replacement of parts to increase the active life of the solution.
11223.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11223.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.1 What to consider when using and disposing of the solution > 37.6.1.1 The high-level design determines how a solution is used and disposed of

11223.sentence: For full disposal, the decommissioning and withdrawal of the full solution should have been designed for.
11223.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11223.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.1 What to consider when using and disposing of the solution > 37.6.1.1 The high-level design determines how a solution is used and disposed of

11224.sentence: In the case of upgrades to or replacement of existing solutions, disruption to ongoing operations and services should be minimised.
11224.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11224.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.1 What to consider when using and disposing of the solution > 37.6.1.2 Maintaining operations and services during disposal

11224.sentence: This should have been understood from the start and defined as a user need, as significant work is often required to achieve such continuity.
11224.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11224.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.1 What to consider when using and disposing of the solution > 37.6.1.2 Maintaining operations and services during disposal

11224.sentence: However, anyone affected should be informed of what this means for them.
11224.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11224.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.1 What to consider when using and disposing of the solution > 37.6.1.2 Maintaining operations and services during disposal

11225.sentence: Planning for use and disposal should start early as soon as the relevant user needs have been identified.
11225.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11225.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.1 Overview

11225.sentence: By the time the high-level design is completed (see Chapter 32: Solution design), the need for associated facilities, tools, logistics and resources for operation should be known.
11225.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11225.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.1 Overview

11226.sentence: Use and disposal requirements should be identified and addressed during the development of the design, not after the solution has been handed over.
11226.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11226.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.2 Plan for use and disposal from the beginning

11226.sentence: The design should account for both the solution itself and any interim states it passes through.
11226.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11226.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.2 Plan for use and disposal from the beginning

11227.sentence: However the changes are categorised and managed, the primary focus should be on ensuring the solution continues to provide a useful and beneficial purpose.
11227.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11227.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.3 Understand maintenance and upgrade needs

11228.sentence: Where appropriate and feasible, continuous and remote monitoring, such as using a digital twin in infrastructure (see Chapter 24: Information and data management) and telemetry, should be considered with thresholds for alerting corrective and preventative action.
11228.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11228.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.4 Understand how the use of the solution is monitored

11229.sentence: Plans for disposal should be reviewed carefully when considering whether to extend the life of, evolve or dispose of a solution.
11229.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11229.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.5 Understand the impacts of disposal

11229.sentence: Financial accounting impacts should also be understood, and early advice sought from the responsible organisation’s finance team.
11229.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11229.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.5 Understand the impacts of disposal

11229.sentence: Any change in asset value has an effect on the organisation’s accounts and should be planned for well in advance.
11229.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11229.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.2 Preparing to use and dispose of the solution > 37.6.2.5 Understand the impacts of disposal

11231.sentence: The use and disposal management framework should be developed before any part of the solution transitions into use.
11231.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11231.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.2 Develop and maintain the use and disposal management framework

11231.sentence: The framework should define the approach to using and disposal of the solution including any processes, methods, tools and techniques to be used.
11231.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11231.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.2 Develop and maintain the use and disposal management framework

11232.sentence: Non-functional performance such as accuracy, security, availability, usability and timeliness should not be neglected.
11232.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11232.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.3 Oversee use and disposal

11232.sentence: The management framework for use and disposal should be monitored to make sure it remains effective and appropriate as the work proceeds.
11232.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11232.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.3 Oversee use and disposal

11233.sentence: The solution should be used, operated and maintained as defined.
11233.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11233.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.4 Use solution

11233.sentence: Records should be kept up to date so that the status of the solution is known at all times as this is fundamental to future decisions that might be needed on changes (see Chapter 22: Change control).
11233.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11233.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.4 Use solution

11234.sentence: Shutdown of the solution should be planned so that impacted stakeholders are aware of what is happening, when and how it could affect them.
11234.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11234.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.5 Plan shutdown and disposal

11234.sentence: This should be managed as organisational or societal change (see Chapter 35: Management of organisational and societal change).
11234.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11234.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.5 Plan shutdown and disposal

11234.sentence: Those accountable for the ultimate disposal of the solution and its parts should plan disposal to be environmentally sustainable.
11234.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11234.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.5 Plan shutdown and disposal

11234.sentence: For physical assets, options such as storing, dismantling, reusing for another purpose, recycling, reprocessing and destroying should be considered.
11234.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11234.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.5 Plan shutdown and disposal

11234.sentence: Data assets should be handled in accordance with government requirements (see Chapter 24: Information and data management).
11234.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11234.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.5 Plan shutdown and disposal

11234.sentence: The choice should take into consideration factors such as costs, disposal sites, environmental impact, health and safety issues, handling, transportation, relocation as well as relevant regulatory requirements.
11234.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11234.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.5 Plan shutdown and disposal

11235.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.6 Shut down solution

11236.sentence: Once the solution or parts of the solution have been shut down, they should be disposed of in accordance with the plan for disposal.
11236.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11236.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.7 Finalise disposal

11236.sentence: Information on the action taken and assets disposed of should be recorded, reported and stored, as this can be important for lessons learned (see Chapter 38: Learning from experience ) and future decision-making, for example on land use.

11236.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.7 Finalise disposal

11237.sentence: Once the solution has been fully disposed of, the management framework should be closed.

11237.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.8 Close the use and disposal management framework

11237.headingPath: Chapter 37: Use and disposal > 37.6 How to manage use and disposal > 37.6.3 Key activities in managing the use and disposal of the solution > 37.6.3.8 Close the use and disposal management framework

11239.sentence: Learning from experience should happen throughout the life cycle of the work, not just at the end.
11239.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11239.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.2 Key points

11239.sentence: Opportunities for improvement should be identified even if they cannot be acted on immediately.
11239.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11239.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.2 Key points

11239.sentence: Lessons should be shared through a range of approaches, from team meetings to learning legacy repositories.
11239.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11239.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.2 Key points

11241.sentence: Everyone in the team should understand how to find and learn from previous lessons, and how to contribute to the lessons process.
11241.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11241.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.4 What is learning from experience?

11241.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11241.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.4 What is learning from experience?

11241.sentence: what action was taken, describing the response to the lesson for the current work When starting and planning work, team members and stakeholders should look for and apply relevant lessons from previous experience, whether from other work in the same portfolio, programme or project or from another organisation.
11241.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11241.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.4 What is learning from experience?

11242.sentence: People in a project delivery role should know how to recognise a potential lesson and where to direct their improvement suggestions and feedback.
11242.actor: People in a project delivery role
11242.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11242.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.5 Who manages learning from experience?

11242.sentence: This should be defined within the governance and management framework and reviewed regularly to check it is being used and is effective.
11242.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11242.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.5 Who manages learning from experience?

11242.sentence: To keep learning from experience effective, too many lessons should not be allocated one owner.
11242.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11242.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.5 Who manages learning from experience?

11244.sentence: If something in the governance and management framework looks wrong or needs better explanation, the owner of that documentation should be told, with suggested amendments or ideas to address the issue.
11244.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11244.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.6 How to learn from experience? > 38.6.1 What to consider when learning from experience > 38.6.1.2 Identifying lessons can be challenging

11245.sentence: Work to implement lessons learned should be managed under change control, like other changes (see Chapter 22: Change control).

11245.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.6 How to learn from experience? > 38.6.1 What to consider when learning from experience > 38.6.1.3 Deciding what lessons need following up

11245.sentence: As with other changes, the lessons manager and owner should consider all proposed changes carefully and only introduce changes after appropriate scrutiny.
11245.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11245.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.6 How to learn from experience? > 38.6.1 What to consider when learning from experience > 38.6.1.3 Deciding what lessons need following up

11246.sentence: Lessons should be assigned to the person best placed to act on them.
11246.sourceTitle: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government
11246.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.6 How to learn from experience? > 38.6.1 What to consider when learning from experience > 38.6.1.4 Deciding who needs to follow up a lesson

11246.sentence: For example, a digital delivery specialist should address feedback on digital matters, while a commercial specialist should own any commercial lessons arising from a procurement.

11246.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.6 How to learn from experience? > 38.6.1 What to consider when learning from experience > 38.6.1.4 Deciding who needs to follow up a lesson

11248.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.6 How to learn from experience? > 38.6.1 What to consider when learning from experience > 38.6.1.6 Being sensitive to realities

11248.headingPath: Chapter 38: Learning from experience > 38.6 How to learn from experience? > 38.6.1 What to consider when learning from experience > 38.6.1.6 Being sensitive to realities

11248.sentence: Care should be taken when writing up and sharing lessons that could be sensitive due to commercial, technical, physical, or people reasons.
